subject: Capacity commit & staffing playbook for upcoming renewal
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
To: Erin Thompson <erin.thompson@averysys.com>, Carlos Diaz <c.diaz@averysys.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, 22 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Capacity commit & staffing playbook for upcoming renewal

Hi Erin / Carlos —

Thanks again for the good conversation last week. As we talked through, your renewal window is approaching and you flagged a likely +2x burst in peak throughput starting in Q4 if the new billing product launches on schedule. I wanted to kick off a short renewal and expansion playbook so we can lock the term amendment, capacity commit, and the QBR cadence with your execs.

High-level asks from our side:
- Confirm the target commit (tokens/month) and preferred term (12 vs 24 months) by Sept 10.
- Align on the primary cost/latency SLO we should optimize for (latency SLO vs lower unit cost).
- Identify exec & technical stakeholders for the QBR (suggested: Erin (exec sponsor), Carlos (platform lead), plus your head of procurement).

Proposed kickoff timeline (draft):
1) This week: internal kickoff and confirm stakeholders (you + us) — finalize attendee list by 8/27.
2) Week of 8/30: model and capacity sizing workshop (SE-run) to validate costs and autoscaling policy.
3) Week of 9/6: mutual action plan (MAP) shared + DocuSign term amendment draft.
4) Target QBR week: 9/20–9/24 (we'll send a poll).

Attachments: I attached a one-page QBR agenda and a preliminary commit summary that maps projected token usage to tiered discounts. These are very draft; we'll iterate after the sizing workshop.

Next steps I'd like to propose:
- Erin/Carlos: confirm who from your side should be present on the sizing call (SE + platform) by Tue 8/24.
- Ben/Marissa/Soojin (cc): can you review the attached commit_summary and weigh in on the proposed discount tiers before Monday?

Thanks — I know timelines are tight given your launch. If simpler, we can lock a short 12-month addendum now, with an option to extend to 24 months at a pre-agreed uplift after QBR.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Director, Customer Success
Redwood Inference
---
Attachment(s): QBR_agenda_v1.pdf (PDF, 0.2MB); commit_summary_20260822.xlsx (Excel, 0.4MB)

From: Erin Thompson <erin.thompson@averysys.com>

Cc: Carlos Diaz <c.diaz@averysys.com>
Date: Sat, 22 Aug 2026 12:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Capacity commit & staffing playbook for upcoming renewal

Kim — thanks for the clear plan and the docs. We're aligned on the need to secure burst headroom for the Q4 product release. A few quick notes:

- We expect the release to increase peak token consumption by ~1.8–2.2x, subject to final load tests on Sept 1.
- Procurement will probably push for a 12-month term with an option to extend; I'll loop in Michael from procurement if you want him on the MAP.
- Stakeholders: I'll be the exec sponsor; Carlos will represent the platform team. I'll confirm the procurement contact (Michael) by 8/24.

For the sizing workshop, can we do a 60-minute session the week of 8/30? Carlos prefers mornings PST. He also asked whether Redwood can share an upfront deployment runbook for the burst scenario so his SREs can review ahead of time.

Happy to do the poll for QBR dates once we lock the sizing session.

—Erin
Erin Thompson
VP, Product
Avery Systems, Inc.

Erin / Carlos —

I'll run the sizing workshop with Soojin leading the SE portion. To make scheduling quick, please choose from these slots (all PST):
- Tue 2026-08-31, 10:00–11:00
- Wed 2026-09-01, 09:00–10:00
- Thu 2026-09-02, 11:00–12:00

If none of these work, tell us preferred times and we'll adjust. I'll attach a short pre-read (QBR_agenda_v1.pdf) and a one-pager runbook for burst handling — share with your SREs ahead of the workshop.

Also, a quick note on commercial approach: we can provision a Dedicated burst pool for Q4 with a 3–6 month uplift pricing short-term, or we can bake the burst into a longer committed tier at a stronger discount. Both approaches keep the autoscaling policy and fallback routing the same; choice is mostly about cashflow and billing predictability.

Attaching: QBR_agenda_v1.pdf; commit_summary_20260822.xlsx

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
